answer: Because the karst ledger attributes every share, the pearl audit publishes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 52% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it pays the summit fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 16 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
